part1.label: North Seattle Design-Build
part1.title: Whole-House Renovations, Builds & Rebuilds
part1.text: Silver Peak Design Build is a residential design-build contractor serving North Seattle and select Eastside communities. We focus on whole-house renovations, builds, rebuilds, and major additions, followed by ADUs, DADUs, and basements. We take select kitchen and bathroom projects when they fit.
Years of residential construction and remodeling experience.

process.label: Project Fit Comes First
process.heading: How Projects Start
process.text: Silver Peak reviews fit before scheduling an in-person technical site assessment.

part1.text: Share your location, project type, goals, and budget range.

part2.text: We confirm the service area, budget, scope, and whether Silver Peak is the right fit.

part3.text: We meet on site to confirm a good working fit, review existing conditions and project feasibility, and present a Design Agreement proposal for the next phase.

part4.text: One company guides two connected phases. Design establishes the layout, key selections, working budget, and material and trade bids. The same team then carries the approved plan through construction.

faq.label: Helpful Answers
faq.heading: Common Renovation Questions
faq.text: Direct answers about whole-house projects, additions, DADUs, ADUs, basements, focused remodels, permits, project fit, and construction planning.

part1.answer: Yes. Silver Peak Design & Build’s contractor registration can be verified directly through Washington State Labor & Industries. [View Silver Peak’s official L&I contractor record](https://secure.lni.wa.gov/verify/Detail.aspx?UBI=603006436&LIC=SILVEPC907LT&SAW=).

part2.answer: A technical site assessment reviews existing conditions, access, structure, utilities, zoning, trees, drainage, side sewer needs, electrical capacity, permits, and project feasibility before design begins.

part3.answer: Building a DADU in Seattle begins with a site assessment covering zoning, lot access, trees, sewer, utilities, electrical capacity, design options, permits, budget, and construction access.

part4.answer: Kitchen design includes layout, traffic flow, work zones, appliance placement, cabinetry, storage, lighting, islands, materials, ventilation, and build coordination.

part5.answer: Bathroom remodeling should address layout, waterproofing, tile, storage, lighting, ventilation, fixtures, accessibility, and durable materials.

part6.answer: An ADU is typically attached to or inside the main home, while a DADU is detached. The right choice depends on lot size, access, zoning, utilities, budget, privacy, and permit feasibility in Seattle.

part7.answer: Schedule a technical site assessment after the initial project-fit review and before finalizing design so zoning, access, utilities, structure, trees, sewer, and permit issues can be identified early.

part8.answer: Well-planned kitchen remodels improve layout, storage, lighting, appliance placement, traffic flow, ventilation, material durability, and everyday usability.

part9.answer: Yes. Bathroom remodeling can include curbless showers, wider clearances, grab bar blocking, slip-resistant materials, better lighting, reachable storage, and comfort-height fixtures.

part10.answer: ADU and DADU planning may require review of electrical capacity, sewer, water service, drainage, heating, ventilation, access, and utility upgrade costs.

part11.answer: Silver Peak focuses on North Seattle neighborhoods including Greenwood, Phinney Ridge, Ballard, Queen Anne, Wallingford, and Fremont, plus select Eastside communities when the project is a good fit.
